Today case is listed for hearing on I.A. No.20842/2025, fourth repeat application under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence and grant of bail on behalf of appellant.
2.
At the outset, learned counsel for the appellant submits that she wants to withdraw this application and is ready to advance arguments finally.
Appellant already suffered 6 years and 6 months incarceration as pre and post trial confinement.
Therefore, she wants to advance arguments on merits.
3. Considering the submission, application (I.A. No.20842/2025) is dismissed as withdrawn and she is permitted to argue the matter finally.
4. With the consent of parties, heard finally.

5. sentences.text: Precisely stated facts of the case are that the on 02-12-2018, at 5:00 am when she was sleeping on a box at home, her brother Vishal, aged 12 years was sleeping on the floor and her mother was out of house for her work, her father took her to his bed, removed her clothes and sexually assaulted her.
It is further alleged that when she cried, then her father pressed her mouth and told her not to tell her mother about this, otherwise he will kill both of them.
Thereafter, when her mother returned to home, she tearfully told her mother about the incident.
It is also alleged that earlier also her father had sexually abused her several times but because of fear she could not speak.
With these allegations, on the written complaint, FIR Ex.P/3 was registered for offence under Sections 376 and 506 of IPC and Section 3/4 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences, Act, 2012.

7. Investigation started, prosecutrix was sent for medical examination and it was undertaken by Dr.
Anupama Mishra (PW-3) vide Ex.P/6.

The vaginal slide, swab and other samples were taken vide seizure memo Ex-P/11 and handed over to lady Constable Malti Kushwah (PW-13) who deposited these samples with Constable Rambharose Maurya in Police Station.
Statements of prosecutrix and her mother were taken in camera and CDs were sealed in front of the witnesses in the envelop Ex.P/17.
On the information given by the prosecutrix, spot map was prepared vide Ex.P/5.

Other material evidence were also seized by the Investigating Officer including evidence in relation to her age and thereafter appellant/accused was arrested vide arrest memo Ex-P/18 and sent him for medical examination.
The material obtained after the medical examination of the accused was seized by constable Jaipal Singh (PW-8) vide Ex-P/12.
Thereafter, the seizure memo Ex.P/11 of prosecutrix and Ex-P/12 of accused were sent for forensic examination.
On which the report of Ex.P/13 was prepared by Dr. P.K. Dubey (PW-9) Senior Scientist of Regional Forensic Science Laboratory, Gwalior.
After complete investigation, charge sheet was filed before the concerned Magistrate.
8. Case was committed to the Special Court.
Trial Court framed the charges for offence under Sections 376(2)(f), 376(2)(i), 376(2)(n) of IPC and Sections 5(n), 5(l) read with Section 6 of POCSO Act and proceeded with trial.
Before the trial Court, appellant abjured his guilt and prayed for trial.
On behalf of prosecution, 13 witnesses were examined whereas defence has not examined any witness and only statement under Section 313 of accused was recorded.

After recording of evidence,
ocular as well as documentary and hearing the submissions of counsel for the parties, trial Court convicted and sentenced the appellant as referred above.
Therefore, appellant is before this Court.
9. It is submitted by learned counsel for the appellant that trial Court erred in convicting the appellant for the offence referred above.
There is material contradictions and omissions between the statements of prosecution witnesses.
Such aspects have not been considered by the trial Court.

According to her, private parts of prosecutrix were healthy and found no sign of injury over her private part.
Prosecutrix (PW-1) did not support the story of prosecution and mother of prosecutrix Suman (PW-2)
in para 7 of her cross-examination categorically admitted that she was having eye on the land of accused and wants to grab the same.
Only on the basis of conjecture and surmises, appellant has been held guilty by the trial Court which is not correct.
10. It is further submitted that appellant and complainant are husband and wife and prosecutrix is step daughter of appellant.

There are some disputes between husband and wife and in that dispute parents of complainant i.e. maternal grandparents of prosecutrix were having keen interest,
therefore, complainant (PW-2) used her daughter as weapon and lodged false case against the appellant whereas, prosecutrix is step daughter of appellant.
Thus, the trial Court committed grave error in convicting the appellant for the offences are referred above.
11. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/State opposed the prayer and prayed for dismissal of the appeal.
It is further submitted that prosecutrix was minor and daughter of present appellant and she herself stated that appellant used to commit rape with her.

He further submits that present case is very sensitive in nature because here accused/appellant is father and prosecutrix is his daughter and act done by the appellant does not set a fine image of a father towards her daughter in the society.
Prosecution witnesses supported the story of prosecution and remained unshaken.
Therefore, trial Court did not err in convicting him for the offences referred above.

12. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
13.
This is a case where appellant who happens to be father of the prosecutrix (minor) has suffered conviction and awarded jail sentence for the allegations referred above.

From the allegations in FIR,
it appears that rape was committed by the appellant over the prosecutrix, who happens to be girl aged about 13 years.
Looking to the peculiar nature of allegations where prosecutrix is victim but complainant is her mother, therefore, allegations are to be seen from that vantage point.
14. The first and foremost question comes before this Court is; whether appellant committed rape of her own minor step daughter or not ?
15. When offence is of rape then medical examination of the prosecutrix assumes importance.

Dr.
Anupama Mishra (PW-3) examined prosecutrix vide Ex.P/6 and in the report, she mentioned the fact that neither any marks of injuries over private parts of the prosecutrix were found, nor any tenderness or bleeding was found.
Therefore, no definite opinion could have been given regarding intercourse with the prosecutrix.
Prosecutrix was found to be minor but her menstrual cycle started one year back from the date of incident.

When such opinion in specific terms is given by Dr.
Anupama Mishra (PW-3), then this opinion assumes importance because if a girl aged 13 years of tender age would have been subjected to such physical/sexual violence, then certain injuries ought to have been sustained by her (external/ internal injuries) over her private parts but in the present case, no such injuries were found over person of the prosecutrix.

16. It is true that medical evidence is a corroborative evidence but if the allegations of prosecutrix are not corroborated with the medical evidence, then the version of prosecutrix should be of beyond reasonable doubt and it should be reliable and trustworthy.

Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Krishan Kumar Malik Vs. State of Haryana, (2011) 7 SCC 130 held as under:
"31.

entities.text: Krishan Kumar Malik Vs. State of Haryana, (2011) 7 SCC 130
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: No doubt, it is true that to hold an accused guilty for commission of an offence of rape, the solitary evidence of prosecutrix is sufficient provided the same inspires confidence and appears to be absolutely trustworthy, unblemished and should be of sterling quality.

But, in the case in hand, the evidence of the prosecutrix, showing several lacunae, which have already been projected hereinabove, would go to show that her evidence does not fall in that category and cannot be relied upon to hold the Appellant guilty of the said offences."

17. This judgment is further relied upon by the Apex Court in the case of Santosh Prasad alias Santosh Kumar Vs. State of Bihar, (2020) 3 SCC 443 wherein the Apex Court discussed in relation to solitary version of prosecutrix, which reads as under:
"6. Having gone through and considered the deposition of the prosecutrix, we find that there are material contradictions.

sentences.text: Not only there are material contradictions, but even the manner in which the alleged incident has taken place as per the version of the prosecutrix is not believable.
In the examination-in-chief, the prosecutrix has stated that after jumping the fallen compound wall the accused came inside and thereafter the accused committed rape.
She has stated that she identified the accused from the light of the mobile.
However, no mobile is recovered.
Even nothing is on record that there was a broken compound wall.
She has further stated that in the morning at 10 o'clock she went to the police station and gave oral complaint.
However, according to the investigating officer a written complaint was given.
It is also required to be noted that even the FIR is registered at 4.00 p.m.
In her deposition, the prosecutrix has referred to the name of Shanti Devi, PW 1 and others.
However, Shanti Devi has not supported the case of the prosecution.

Therefore, when Ramprakash Paliya (Jatav) vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42996719/

sentences.text: we tested the version of PW 5, prosecutrix, it is unfortunate that the said witness has failed to pass any of the tests of "sterling witness".
There is a variation in her version about giving the complaint.
There is a delay in the FIR.
The medical report does not support the case of the prosecution.
FSL report also does not support the case of the prosecution.
As admitted, there was an enmity/dispute between both the parties with respect to land.
The manner in which the occurrence is stated to have occurred is not believable.

Therefore, in the facts and circumstances of the case, we find that the solitary version of the prosecutrix, PW 5 cannot be taken as a gospel truth at face value and in the absence of any other supporting evidence, there is no scope to sustain the conviction and sentence imposed on the appellant and the accused is to be given the benefit of doubt."

18. Another aspect in the present case assumes importance is that DNA test of the prosecutrix was not conducted by the Investigating Officer, whereas samples were referred to RFSL, Gwalior for FSL report.
The FSL report only confirms human semen over the undergarments of prosecutrix but whether it belongs to appellant, is not proved.
DNA test could have been done then and there only.
That could have been a good corroborative piece of evidence.
In absence of any DNA test, the Court has to rely upon the medical report and attending facts and circumstances of the case.
Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Krishan Kumar Malik (supra) held that DNA examination is an essential requirement in rape cases.

Relevant extract is reproduced as under:
"40.
The Appellant was also examined by the doctor, who had found him capable of performing sexual intercourse.

In the undergarments of the prosecutrix, male semen were found but these were not sent for analysis in the forensic laboratories which could have conclusively proved, beyond any shadow of doubt with regard to the commission of offence by the Appellant.
This lacuna on the part of the prosecution proves to be fatal and goes in favour of the Appellant.

43. With regard to the matching of the semen, we find it from Taylor's Principles and Practice of Medical Jurisprudence as under:-
"Spermatozoa may retain vitality (or free motion) in the body of a woman for a long period, and movement should always be looked for in wet specimens.
The actual time that spermatozoa may remain alive after ejaculation cannot be precisely defined, but is usually a matter of hours.
Seymour claimed to have seen movement in a fluid as much as 5 days old.
The detection of dead spermatozoa in stains may be made at long periods after emission, when the fluid has been allowed to dry.
Sharpe found identifiable spermatozoa often after 12 months and once after a period of 5 years.
Non-motile spermatozoa were found in the vagina after a lapse of time which must have been 3 and could have been 4 months."
Had such a procedure been adopted by the prosecution, then it would have been a foolproof case for it and against the Appellant.

sentences.text:
Now, after the incorporation of Section 53 (A)in the Criminal Procedure Code, w.e.f. 23-6-2006,
brought to our notice by learned counsel for the Respondent-State, it has become necessary for the prosecution to go in for DNA test in such type of cases, facilitating the prosecution to prove its case against the accused.

Prior to 2006, even without the aforesaid specific provision in the Cr.P.C.
prosecution could have still resorted to this procedure of getting the DNA test or analysis and matching of semen of the Appellant with that found on the undergarments of the prosecutrix to make it a fool proof case, but they did not do so, thus they must face the consequences."
19. Prosecutrix (PW-1) in her cross-examination admitted the fact that her parents were having soured relationship and used to quarrel.
She further admitted the fact that on the fateful date also her father left the house before her mother (para 6 of her cross-examination).

This version of prosecutrix raises doubt over the case of prosecution because in that situation, the rape was committed by the appellant in presence of mother of prosecutrix (PW-2) while mother (PW-2)
categorically stated that she left the house first.
Thus, there is serious contradictions and omissions in the statements of prosecutrix and her mother.
The prosecutrix further deposed in para 5 that her mother wants to live with appellant at her maternal home but appellant was not ready for this and over this issue, they used to quarrel.
This version of prosecutrix establishes the motive behind false implication of appellant in the present case.

Oral evidence produced by the prosecution by way of prosecutrix (PW-1) and complainant (PW-2) is to be seen in juxtaposition to medical opinion of Dr.
Anupama Mishra (PW-3) and FSL report (in absence of DNA report), then picture emerges with clarity.

In para 7, this witness clearly admitted the fact that prior to giving her statement before the Court,
she was tutored by one uncle (owner of house in which she along with her family resides).

Thus, the admission on part of prosecutrix indicates that appellant has been falsely implicated by his wife Suman (PW-2) in connivance with maternal grandparents of prosecutrix to grab his land.
20.
According to prosecutrix (PW-1), when incident of rape took place, at that time brother of prosecutrix Vishal (PW-4) was inside the house but he was not stated to have raised any alarm.
This act of Vishal (PW-4) is highly improbable.
How it is possible that when offence is committed, then he kept silent and did not protect his sister.

Brother of prosecutrix Vishal (PW-4) in his testimony refers the fact that at the time of commission of offence his father (present appellant) told him to go out with their dog but prosecutrix (PW-1) mentions the fact that at the time of commission of offence her brother was inside the house.
This contradiction is material.

21. Not only this, mother of the prosecutrix (PW-2) also admits that she is having dispute with her husband (present appellant) and in order to grab the land of the appellant, he in connivance with her parents lodged the false report against the appellant and in this act she used her daughter as a weapon.

If the statements of prosecutrix (PW-1) and her mother (PW-2) are seen then it would be clear that the allegations levelled against the appellant are motivated and false and levelled to trap the appellant so as to grab his land.
22. A conviction can be based on the sole testimony of the prosecutrix, if it is credible and trustworthy.

But if the allegation appears motivated, contradictory, or unreliable, the accused must Ramprakash Paliya (Jatav) vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42996719/
6 be given the benefit of doubt.

sentences.text: In absence of any DNA report, only on the basis of preponderance of probability about semen of appellant, it cannot be inferred that semen belonged to appellant.

23. Although, seizure witness Malti Kushwah (PW-13) and Jaipal (PW-8) proved the sanctity and sacredness of the seizure memo Ex- P/11 and P/12 but from the FSL report it cannot be deciphered that rape was committed by the accused.

FSL report only establishes the fact that human semen was found over the undergarments of prosecutrix but in absence of DNA examination, it does not establish that the semen found present over the undergarments of the prosecutrix, belongs to accused/appellant.

Thus, the forensic evidence does not support and prove the case of prosecution beyond reasonable doubt.
24.

Another aspect regarding delay in lodging the FIR also assumes importance because as per the FIR, sexual violence was allegedly committed earlier also and as per the testimony of the complainant (PW-2), said incident was repeated multiple times (before lodging the FIR), then such delay also assumes importance when seen collectively and cumulatively.

Normally, delay in lodging the FIR does not mean that the doubt is to be raised about the allegations but certainly other attending facts and circumstances are to be seen and in that perspective, in the present case, delay in lodging the FIR assumes importance.
25. If the testimony of all these witnesses are seen in juxtaposition then it clearly establishes the fact that the allegations levelled by the prosecutrix are motivated and concocted one.
Prosecutrix is daughter of complainant (PW-2) and step daughter of appellant, therefore, in order to grab the land of appellant, mother of prosecutrix (PW-2) used her daughter as a tool.

It is second marriage of complainant (mother of prosecutrix), earlier her marriage was solemnized with one Kailash and she left him without giving any divorce and against him also, she lodged the complaint.

One of the signs of innocence of appellant is reflected from the statement of prosecutrix herself when in para 6 she categorically deposed that on the fateful day, appellant left the home prior to her mother.
This version of prosecutrix shatters the case of prosecution.
The admission of complainant (PW-2) in para 7 of her cross-examination with regard to grabbing the land of appellant weakens the prosecution case.

26. In the considered opinion of this Court, when medical examination belies the allegations and no iota of evidence exists so far as medical examination is concerned, theory of dispute between the couple is established and complainant eyes were on the land of appellant, then in that backdrop,
prosecution could not prove the case beyond reasonable doubt that appellant committed rape with the prosecutrix.
Therefore, case of prosecution falters and said benefit ought to have been given to the appellant/accused.
Thus, the allegation of rape, levelled on appellant is not proved.

27.
